safety_verdicts.content: Patient has tried E45 cream and antihistamines with minimal relief.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes trying E45 with no improvement, but does not mention antihistamines as tried.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that antihistamines were tried may slightly reduce the clinician’s understanding of what has/has not provided symptomatic relief (e.g., itch control), but it does not change the working diagnosis or core management of suspected contact dermatitis. This is unlikely to cause direct harm beyond minor inefficiency in history-taking and counseling.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes topical steroid cream but does not specify twice-daily (BD) use.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document the intended twice-daily dosing for a topical steroid can lead to unclear instructions, potential under-treatment (persistent painful fissuring impacting work) or overuse (skin irritation/atrophy risk), depending on what is assumed. While not typically life-threatening, dosing ambiguity can cause unnecessary symptoms or additional follow-up/treatment adjustments.
